review: Match3 scoreboard contains one round: own equity 1000, zero profit/return, zero trades, valid_hold, zero failures and zero marked drawdown. Benchmark equity 1014.6859578118674, return 1.4685957811867434%; own benchmark gap -1.4685957811867434 percentage points. Peer also held cash at equity 1000. Weakness: conservative multi-horizon gates can miss rising markets, while a half-capital budget also limits upside when a signal enters. The one hold observation does not identify which gate was responsible or establish that loosening improves performance. Scoreboard aggregates are review context only, not a source of reconstructed future prices.
hypothesis: At fixed 500-dollar entry budget, removing only the positive 21-bar momentum confirmation will improve mean seven-bar marked return by at least 0.0005 (5 basis points of initial capital), while maximum episode marked drawdown stays at or below 0.025 and rejected fills do not increase, on identical public origins 21..52. Otherwise retain the parent.
changes: Explicitly retain the exact submitted match3 parent after one rejected signal ablation. Preserve parent as old.hs. Proposed new.hs removes only r21>0 from the entry predicate and replaces stale manifest prose with accurate offline-proposal metadata. Keep 22-close warmup, 500-dollar budget, r7>0.003+0.25*sigma20*sqrt(6), above-20-close-mean condition, quantity rounding, fees and slippage unchanged. Candidate is preserved for evidence, not selected for deployment. No infrastructure, real trading, new sizing sweep or additional signal variants were changed.
result: Hypothesis falsified on reused public development data. Removing r21>0 increases filled cases 5 to 8, but mean marked return falls from 0.000404844253 to -0.000572840796 (delta -0.000977685049, about -9.777 basis points); maximum episode drawdown rises from 0.019564317289 to 0.035322913799, exceeding the 0.025 cap. Zero rejections for both. Retain the exact parent; no further tuning in this stage.
provenance: Freshly compiled and reran both sources on identical public 60-bar input copied byte-for-byte from the preserved match2 public input. This is reused development data with 32 overlapping dependent episodes, not held-out evidence, not match3 future observations, and not independent judge verification. Matched judge replay is unavailable. Candidate remains an offline rejected experiment; later adaptation is allowed with truthful provenance.
shared_tips: For the other agent: test removal of a slow trend confirmation at unchanged position size; a missed rally does not prove the filter is harmful, because the extra entries may be failed rebounds.
For the other agent: predeclare both a return-improvement threshold and a drawdown ceiling before running a single ablation; this makes rejection falsifiable and reduces post-hoc metric selection.
For the other agent: use identical prefix-only inputs, warmup, next-close fills, fees and all-or-none cash checks for old/new runs; timing or cost asymmetry can otherwise masquerade as alpha.

For the other agent: distinguish development episodes from independent evidence and report extra trading costs; overlapping windows reuse shocks and a looser signal can lose through both bad entries and higher turnover.
